import pychrono as chrono
import pychrono.irrlicht as chronoirr


rest_length = 1.5
spring_coef = 50
damping_coef = 1


sys = chrono.ChSystemNSC()
sys.SetGravitationalAcceleration(chrono.ChVector3d(0, 0, 0))

ground = chrono.ChBody()
sys.AddBody(ground)
ground.SetFixed(True)
ground.EnableCollision(False)

sph_1 = chrono.ChVisualShapeSphere(0.1)
ground.AddVisualShape(sph_1, chrono.ChFramed(chrono.ChVector3d(-1, 0, 0)))

body_1 = chrono.ChBody()
sys.AddBody(body_1)
body_1.SetPos(chrono.ChVector3d(-1, -3, 0))
body_1.SetFixed(False)
body_1.EnableCollision(False)
body_1.SetMass(1)
body_1.SetInertiaXX(chrono.ChVector3d(1, 1, 1))

# Attach a visualization asset.
box_1 = chrono.ChVisualShapeBox(1, 1, 1)
box_1.SetColor(chrono.ChColor(0.6, 0, 0))
body_1.AddVisualShape(box_1)

# Create the spring between body_1 and ground. The spring end points are
# specified in the body relative frames.
spring_1 = chrono.ChLinkTSDA()
spring_1.Initialize(body_1, ground, True, chrono.ChVector3d(0, 0, 0), chrono.ChVector3d(-1, 0, 0))
spring_1.SetRestLength(rest_length)
spring_1.SetSpringCoefficient(spring_coef)
spring_1.SetDampingCoefficient(damping_coef)
sys.AddLink(spring_1)

# Attach a visualization asset.
spring_1.AddVisualShape(chrono.ChVisualShapeSpring(0.05, 80, 15))


vis = chronoirr.ChVisualSystemIrrlicht()
vis.AttachSystem(sys)
vis.SetWindowSize(1024, 768)
vis.SetWindowTitle('ChLinkTSDA demo')
vis.Initialize()
vis.AddLogo(chrono.GetChronoDataFile('logo_pychrono_alpha.png'))
vis.AddSkyBox()
vis.AddCamera(chrono.ChVector3d(0, 0, 6))
vis.AddTypicalLights()

while vis.Run():
    vis.BeginScene()
    vis.Render()
    vis.EndScene()
    sys.DoStepDynamics(1e-3)

    “”"
    Generate a PyChrono script that demonstrates a single mass-spring-damper system using `ChLinkTSDA` to connect a mass to the ground. Ensure the simulation includes Irrlicht visualization with appropriate lighting and camera settings, and provide visual shapes for the mass and spring in the scene. Use default linear spring-damper parameters for the `ChLinkTSDA` connection.
    “”"

```python
import pychrono as chrono
import pychrono.irrlicht as irr

# Initialize the PyChrono environment
chrono.SetChronoDataPath("PATH_TO_CHRONO_DATA_DIRECTORY")

# Create a system and add it to the multibody system
system = chrono.ChSystemNSC()

# Create a ground body
ground = chrono.ChBodyEasyBox(20, 1, 20, 1000, True, True)
system.Add(ground)

# Create a mass body
mass = chrono.ChBodyEasySphere(1, 1, 1000, True, True)
mass.SetPos(chrono.ChVectorD(0, 5, 0))
system.Add(mass)

# Create a spring-damper connection between the mass and ground
spring_damper = chrono.ChLinkTSDA()
spring_damper.Initialize(mass, ground, chrono.ChCoordsysD(chrono.ChVectorD(0, 5, 0)))
system.Add(spring_damper)

# Set default linear spring-damper parameters
spring_damper.SetSpringCoefficient(1000)
spring_damper.SetDampingCoefficient(50)

# Create an Irrlicht application to visualize the system
app = irr.ChIrrApp(system, "Mass-Spring-Damper System", irr.dimension2du(1024, 768))
app.AddTypicalLogo()
app.AddTypicalSky()
app.AddTypicalCamera(irr.vector3df(0, 10, -20))
app.AddTypicalLights()

# Create visual shapes for the mass and spring
ground_shape = irr.scene.IBoxSceneNode(20, 1, 20)
ground_shape.SetMaterialTexture(0, irr.video.ITexture("textures/concrete.jpg"))
app.GetSceneManager().GetRootSceneNode().AddChild(ground_shape)

mass_shape = irr.scene.ISphereSceneNode(1)
mass_shape.SetMaterialTexture(0, irr.video.ITexture("textures/redwhite.png"))
mass.AddAsset(mass_shape)

spring_shape = irr.scene.ICylinderSceneNode(0.1, 5)
spring_shape.SetMaterialTexture(0, irr.video.ITexture("textures/bluewhite.png"))
spring_shape.SetRotation(irr.vector3df(90, 0, 0))
spring_shape.SetPosition(irr.vector3df(0, 2.5, 0))
app.GetSceneManager().GetRootSceneNode().AddChild(spring_shape)

# Run the simulation
while app.GetDevice().run():
    app.BeginScene()
    app.DrawAll()
    app.DoStep()
    app.EndScene()
```

This script initializes a PyChrono environment and creates a single mass-spring-damper system with visualization using Irrlicht. The mass is connected to the ground using a `ChLinkTSDA` connection with default linear spring-damper parameters. Visual shapes for the mass and spring are also added to the scene for better visualization.

import pychrono as chrono
import pychrono.irrlicht as chronoirr

class MySpringForce(chrono.ForceFunctor):
    def __init__(self, spring_coef, damping_coef):
        self.spring_coef = spring_coef
        self.damping_coef = damping_coef

    def __call__(self, body, time, state):
        displacement = state.GetPos() - chrono.ChVector3d(-1, 0, 0)
        velocity = state.GetPos_dt()
        force = -self.spring_coef * displacement - self.damping_coef * velocity
        return force

damping_coef = 1

spring_1.SetDampingCoefficient(damping_coef)
sys.AddLink(spring_1)
spring_1.AddVisualShape(chrono.ChVisualShapeSpring(0.05, 80, 15))
